Yes. In the provided supplementary tables, feminizing GAHT-associated proteins substantially overlap with sex-associated proteins from the general population.

Using the shared Olink-protein universe in Supplementary Table 5 (2711 proteins), 213 proteins were flagged as both sex-associated and GAHT-effect proteins. For CPA, all 213 significant shared-universe GAHT proteins fell in this overlap set (Fisher's exact p = 1.864e-319). For SPIRO, 35 of 81 significant shared-universe GAHT proteins were in the overlap set, which was also far more than expected by chance (odds ratio = 10.03, Fisher's exact p = 2.265e-18).

The overlap is not only by membership but also often by direction. Among overlap proteins with non-missing sex-effect estimates, 110/173 (63.6%) CPA effects and 114/173 (65.9%) SPIRO effects had the same sign as the female-versus-male effect; both exceed chance expectation. The effect sizes were positively correlated with the female effect direction as well (Spearman rho = 0.489 for CPA and 0.534 for SPIRO).

Examples of concordant overlap include decreases in male-associated proteins such as SPINT3, INSL3, EDDM3B, TEX101, ACRV1, PROK1 and MSMB, plus increases in female-associated proteins such as LEP and PRL. Not every protein was direction-concordant, so feminizing GAHT partially, but not perfectly, recapitulated general-population sex-associated proteomic differences.
